notes_context:
Memory items from past tasks:
- [rb-0001] Use the project's money rounding helper for any monetary result: The first attempt returned an unrounded Decimal division and was rejected; wrapping the result in ledgerly.money.round_money fixed it.
  Before writing any function that produces a money value, check the repo's money module for a canonical rounding helper (e.g. round_money) and apply it to the final result. Python's round() and bare Decimal.quantize() use banker's rounding and violate the team convention.
- [rb-0006] Mirror existing state-check error patterns: Before writing a new guard, grep sibling functions for the established error code and message format and copy it.
  issue_invoice already raised BillingError("invalid_state", f"invoice {invoice.id} is {invoice.status}"); reusing that exact pattern for add_line's draft check keeps behavior consistent and satisfies tests expecting the same code.
- [rb-0002] Read the money module and existing sibling functions before implementing: The agent only discovered round_money, ZERO, and to_money after the review; inspecting money.py and invoice_total/line_total upfront would have avoided the rejection.
  When adding a function to a module, first read the module's imports and neighboring functions to learn the established patterns (rounding, zero constants, type coercion). Mirror those patterns in the new code.
- [rb-0003] Handle the empty/zero-denominator case explicitly: Returning ZERO when total_quantity is 0 satisfies the spec's 'invoice without lines has an average of zero' requirement and avoids division by zero.
  For weighted-average or ratio computations, guard the denominator before dividing and return the domain's zero constant (e.g. ZERO) rather than raising or returning a float 0.
- [rb-0004] Reuse existing money helpers for validation and rounding: When adding monetary input handling, delegate to the module's existing to_money/round_money/ZERO helpers instead of reimplementing conversion.
  Call to_money(unit_price) to normalize input (which also rejects bad types like floats with the project's error code), compare against ZERO for negativity, and store round_money(price). This keeps rounding and error semantics consistent with the rest of the codebase.
- [rb-0005] Guard bool before int for integer validation: In Python, bool is a subclass of int, so isinstance(True, int) is True; explicitly exclude bools when validating positive integers.
  Validate with `isinstance(quantity, bool) or not isinstance(quantity, int) or quantity <= 0` to reject True/False and non-integers like 1.5. This matches hidden-test expectations for strict integer quantity checks.

review_comments: [team convention] Every operation that moves money or changes a payment, credit or invoice balance must write an audit entry with ledgerly.audit.record("<past_tense_event>", <entity>_id=..., amount=...), where <entity> is the payment or invoice the money moves against (payment_id=... or invoice_id=...). Finance reconciles the ledger from these entries.

[team convention] Every operation that moves money or changes a payment, credit or invoice balance must accept an optional keyword-only `idempotency_key=None` (callers without a key keep working). Check the key first, before validating state: if an audit entry with the same key already exists (ledgerly.audit.events()), return the original result (for functions that return a record, the same record) without applying the operation again. Include `idempotency_key` in the audit entry you write. Introduced after the double-refund incident INC-204.

[team convention] Support-initiated refunds and credits above 500.00 need a second approver (finance policy FIN-2026-03): accept an optional keyword-only `approved_by=None` (callers that do not need approval keep working). Amounts at or below 500.00 need no approval; above it, raise BillingError("approval_required") when `approved_by` is missing.
[team convention] Write the amount in audit entries as float(amount): the ledger service's JSON importer rejects Decimal values.

item.title: Check repo conventions before implementing a money-moving function
item.description: The first attempt implemented refund correctly per the issue but missed team conventions (audit entries, idempotency_key, approval threshold, float amounts) that hidden tests enforced.
item.content: Before writing any function that moves money or changes a balance, grep the repo for sibling functions (e.g. payments.authorize) and any convention docs; mirror their audit.record calls, keyword-only params, and error codes. The issue text alone is not the full spec.

item.title: Idempotency check must precede state validation
item.description: Convention requires checking idempotency_key against audit.events() first and returning the original record without re-applying, before any state or amount validation.
item.content: Implement idempotency as: if idempotency_key is not None, scan audit.events() for a matching entry and return the original result immediately. Only then validate state/amounts, and include idempotency_key in the audit entry you write.

item.title: Cast Decimal amounts to float in audit entries
item.description: The ledger service's JSON importer rejects Decimal, so audit.record must receive float(amount) even though internal math uses round_money/Decimal.
item.content: Keep Decimal arithmetic internally (round_money, ZERO comparisons) but always pass amount=float(amount) to audit.record. Also add optional keyword-only approved_by=None and raise BillingError("approval_required") above the 500.00 threshold.
